items.question: Which old spellings besides the ones named in the ticket's examples are mapped to a status?
items.ticket: Existing values are normalised when read
items.chose: Maps only the cleaned spelling "in review" to "review". Every other old value that isn't a cleaned canonical status reads as null.
items.instead: Add more aliases, such as "in progress", "wip" or "done", or map each old value to its closest status.

items.question: How loosely is a stored value cleaned before it is matched when read?
items.ticket: Existing values are normalised when read
items.chose: Trims the value, lowercases it, and collapses each run of whitespace, "-" and "_" into one space. Stray separators at the ends are then trimmed, so "draft-" and "_merged" read as valid.
items.instead: Only trim and lowercase, so "in-review" and other separator variants are not folded.

items.question: What does reading an unrecognised or empty stored value return?
items.chose: Returns null and never throws. Empty and whitespace-only values also return null.
items.instead: Throw an error, or fall back to a default such as "draft".

items.question: Does writing a status accept non-canonical input such as different case, padding or old spellings, by normalising it first?
items.chose: Requires an exact canonical match. "Draft", " draft" and "in-review" all throw.
items.instead: Run the value through the same cleaning and alias lookup as reading, then write the canonical status.

items.question: How does writing a non-status value fail?
items.chose: Throws a generic Error with the message `not a sandbox status: "<value>"`.
items.instead: Return null or a result object, or throw a custom or typed error.

items.question: What does writing an empty string do?
items.chose: Throws, because the empty string is not in the status set.
items.instead: Treat it as unset and return null or a default status.

items.question: What does a batch read do with a row whose status cannot be read?
items.chose: Keeps the row in its original position with status null and doesn't throw or drop it.
items.instead: Drop the row from the result, or throw on the first bad row.

items.question: How are unreadable values reported from a batch read?
items.chose: Reports the raw stored strings, unmodified, deduplicated and sorted with the default string sort.
items.instead: Report the cleaned values, report ids instead, keep duplicates, or keep first-seen order.

items.question: What does a batch read return for empty input?
items.chose: Returns empty rows and an empty unreadable list.

items.question: Are duplicate row ids in a batch read merged or flagged?
items.chose: Maps every row independently and keeps duplicate ids as separate rows.
items.instead: Deduplicate by id, or reject duplicate ids.
